_comment: Water need from wording on pages already cited by each plant (checked 2026-10-22). level: low | medium | high. quote = the wording relied on. Applied by apply_wording.py. Plants with a USDA minimum are never listed here.
hops: This vine is drought tolerant and needs good drainage.
maypop: Although this vine is tolerant of drought
rosemary: Rosemary is drought tolerant once established
roman-chamomile: Provide part sun to full sun in well-drained, moist to dry soils; Resistance To Challenges: Drought
wild-strawberry: fertile, moist to dry, well-drained soils; Resistance To Challenges: Drought
borage: once established does well on soils that are dry
creeping-thyme: It is drought tolerant and prefers average to dry medium moisture.
oregano: Oregano plants tolerate heat and drought (NC State); compact and drought tolerant (RHS)
thyme: It is frost and drought-tolerant (NC State); Thyme is drought tolerant and rarely needs watering (RHS)
garden-sage: well-drained, medium to dry soils (NC State); Sage is drought tolerant once established (RHS)
tarragon: Tarragon is drought tolerant once established (RHS); best suited to dry, sunny, well-drained soil (NC State)
winter-savory: easy to grow in sandy, well-drained soil and dry or medium levels of moisture; Resistance To Challenges: Drought, Dry Soil
sweet-marjoram: excellent drought and heat tolerance once established (NC State); drought tolerant once established (RHS)
anise-hyssop: mesic to dry conditions; Drought Tolerant Garden
chives: Chives are drought tolerant once established (UW); deer and drought resistant (NC State)
red-currant: Currants are tolerant of dry conditions, no need for irrigation in WI.
goji: once established, will tolerate wind, salt-laden air and drought
english-lavender: Drought tolerant; Resistance To Challenges: Drought, Dry Soil
sweet-chestnut: prefers full sun, dry or moist soil and can tolerate drought
jujube: It will tolerate poor soils and drought (NC State); quite tolerant to drought (NMSU)
olive: They are drought tolerant once established.
loquat: Easy to grow, tolerates alkaline soil, drought
common-myrtle: Resistance To Challenges: Drought, Dry Soil; Drought Tolerant Garden
strawberry-tree: tolerant of full sun to partial shade, salt, and drought once established
pea: Peas grow best in full sun and moist, well-drained soil.
sweet-cicely: Grow in moderately fertile, moist but well-drained soil
blackthorn: Grows in any moist well-drained soil in full sun
damson: moist, but well-drained soil (RHS); full sun with medium moisture and good drainage (NC State)
horseradish: in amended well-drained moist garden soil
onion: should be planted in moist but well-drained fertile loose soils
walking-onion: in moist, fertile, well-drained sandy loams
asparagus: moist, organic, sandy soil with good drainage
hazel: Grow in any moist but well-drained soil in sun or partial shade
japanese-quince: spots with well-drained soil and medium moisture
elder: Plant in moist, high organic matter, well-drained soil
plum: fertile moist well-drained soil; medium moist, organic soil with good drainage; moist, but well-drained soil
peach: moist, fertile, well-drained, acidic soil (NC State); moist, but well-drained soil (RHS)
lemon-verbena: full sun in well-drained moist fertile light soils
arctic-kiwi: fertile, evenly moist soil (NC State); The plants need constant moisture, but not soggy soil (UW)
runner-bean: consistently moist, organically rich, well drained soil (NC State); thirsty plants ... regular watering is usually required (RHS)
cranberry: This plant is intolerant of heat and drought (NC State); Cranberries require moist, acidic, lime-free soil (RHS)
radish: consistent moisture is needed (NC State); Keep the soil consistently moist (RHS)
garlic: Garlic is shallow rooted and is sensitive to dry soil so irrigation is important.
bee-balm: Bee balms like an even supply of moisture during the growing season.
strawberry: they need to be watered frequently with 1 inch of water
haskap: Irrigation required under normal Ontario conditions (OMAFRA); Ensure that soils remain moist ... not drought-tolerant (USU)
fig: Fig trees need a steady supply of moisture throughout the growing season (RHS); moist soil (NC State)
banana: Keep the soil moist (NC State); Lack of water at any time may cause a reduction in fruit number and size (UF/IFAS)
lemon: They need plenty of water during the growing season
persian-lime: kept moist but drains well; watered regularly especially during times of drought
ginger: water sparingly until the plant starts to grow, then water and fertilize regularly
